feed.subtitle: We study the mechanisms of gut remodeling and regeneration across developmental disorders, acquired intestinal injury, and systemic disease states at the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre, Macau University of Science and Technology.

entry.content:
The Bo Li Laboratory at the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC), Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST), is pleased to announce the international symposium “Frontiers in Science: A Youth-Led Vanguard International Symposium on Healthy Aging,” to be held in Macao from November 1 to 4, 2026.

The symposium is a youth-led initiative that brings together early-career researchers and leading scientists to explore the frontiers of healthy aging research. The program spans fundamental mechanisms of aging, age-related diseases, and emerging therapeutic and regenerative strategies, with a focus on interdisciplinary approaches and the translation of research into improved health across the life course.

The four-day program features keynote lectures, invited talks, and presentations from young investigators addressing topics at the intersection of aging, stem cell biology, regenerative medicine, and related disciplines. By placing young scientists at the forefront of the scientific program, the symposium aims to foster the next generation of leaders in healthy aging research and to strengthen international collaboration among emerging and established researchers.

Further details on the program and participation will be shared as the event approaches. We warmly welcome colleagues interested in healthy aging and regenerative medicine to join us in Macao this November.

entry.title: Postdoctoral Fellow Dorothy Lee Receives Michael Höllwarth Prize at ISPSR 2026

link.title: Postdoctoral Fellow Dorothy Lee Receives Michael Höllwarth Prize at ISPSR 2026

entry.content:
Postdoctoral Fellow Dorothy Lee from the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC) at Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST) was awarded the Michael Höllwarth Prize at the International Symposium on Pediatric Surgical Research (ISPSR) 2026, held in Venice, Italy, from October 8 to 10, 2026. The prize recognizes outstanding research contributions presented at the symposium.

Dr. Lee received the award for her presentation on intestinal injury, tissue repair, and regenerative medicine in neonatal and paediatric disease. Her work reflects the PRMRC’s ongoing efforts to integrate stem cell biology, organoid models, and regenerative therapeutic strategies to address severe neonatal and paediatric intestinal diseases.

ISPSR is a leading international forum dedicated to advancing research in pediatric surgery, bringing together surgeons, scientists, and researchers from around the world to share the latest findings in congenital malformations, neonatal surgical diseases, tissue injury and repair, and translational research.

The Michael Höllwarth Prize is awarded in honor of Professor Michael Höllwarth, a distinguished figure in pediatric surgical research, and recognizes young investigators for excellence in scientific research and presentation. This recognition highlights the growing international visibility of the Centre’s research in pediatric surgical diseases and regenerative medicine.

Figure 1. Postdoctoral Fellow Dorothy Lee receives the Michael Höllwarth Prize at the ISPSR 2026 in Venice, Italy.

entry.title: MUST Signs Memorandum of Understanding with Nazarbayev University to Strengthen International Medical Collaboration

link.title: MUST Signs Memorandum of Understanding with Nazarbayev University to Strengthen International Medical Collaboration

entry.content:
On October 5, 2026, Professor Paul Kwong-Hang Tam, Vice President of Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST), and Dr. Bo Li, Assistant Professor at the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC), represented MUST at the international medical seminar “Global Medical Frontiers: Innovation, Resilience and Sharing” held in Astana, Kazakhstan. The seminar was jointly organized by the GX Foundation, the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan, and Nazarbayev University (NU). During the event, MUST and NU formally signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), opening new opportunities for collaboration in medical education, scientific research, and talent development.

The seminar brought together medical experts and healthcare professionals from Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, Kazakhstan, and other countries and regions. Discussions focused on clinical innovation, healthcare systems management, public health, medical education, and international cooperation. The event was attended by Mr. Leung Chun-ying, Vice Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference and Chairman of the GX Foundation, alongside representatives from government agencies, universities, and healthcare institutions.

Signing of the Memorandum of Understanding

During the seminar, MUST and Nazarbayev University held a formal MoU signing ceremony. Professor Paul Kwong-Hang Tam, Vice President of MUST, and Professor Ng Huck-Hui, Vice President for Medicine and Dean of the School of Medicine at Nazarbayev University, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective institutions.

Figure 1. Signing ceremony of the Memorandum of Understanding between Macau University of Science and Technology and Nazarbayev University.

Under the MoU, the two universities will strengthen cooperation in education, scientific research, and academic and cultural exchanges. The agreement provides a framework for exploring joint research initiatives, faculty and researcher exchanges, and collaborative talent development, laying the foundation for a long-term institutional partnership. This agreement represents an important step in expanding MUST’s academic partnerships with leading research universities in Central Asia and creates new opportunities for deeper collaboration in medical education and research innovation.

Two Presentations on Medical Innovation and Education

Professor Tam delivered two presentations at the seminar, addressing advances in pediatric minimally invasive surgery and regenerative medicine, as well as medical education and talent development.

During the morning session on clinical technologies, Professor Tam presented “Minimally Invasive Surgery and Regenerative Medicine for Infants and Children,” highlighting research advances and clinical applications in these fields and emphasizing the potential of minimally invasive surgical techniques and regenerative medicine to improve the treatment and care of infants and children.

Figure 2. Professor Paul Kwong-Hang Tam, Vice President of MUST, delivers his presentation on “Minimally Invasive Surgery and Regenerative Medicine for Infants and Children.”

In the afternoon session on medical education and workforce development, Professor Tam delivered a presentation entitled “Building a Medical and Health Education System with Limited Resources,” sharing MUST’s experiences and achievements in medical education, talent development, and medical research, while exchanging perspectives with international colleagues on future directions and opportunities for collaboration in medical education.

Figure 3. Professor Paul Tam delivers his presentation entitled “Building a Medical and Health Education System with Limited Resources.”

Visit to Nazarbayev University’s School of Medicine and Research Facilities

During the visit, the MUST delegation also toured Nazarbayev University’s School of Medicine and its laboratory animal research facility (Vivarium), gaining insights into the university’s medical research activities, experimental animal facilities, and research infrastructure.

Dr. Bo Li engaged in academic discussions with faculty members and researchers at Nazarbayev University. The exchanges covered basic medical research, disease mechanisms, regenerative medicine, and research infrastructure development. Both sides also explored potential opportunities for future collaboration in joint research projects, technical exchanges, and the training of early-career researchers.

Strengthening Partnerships under the Belt and Road Initiative

Kazakhstan is an important partner in the Belt and Road Initiative. The signing of the MoU between MUST and Nazarbayev University further strengthens academic ties between the two institutions and creates new opportunities for universities in Macao to participate in international research and educational cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative.

Looking ahead, MUST will continue to leverage Macao’s unique position as a bridge connecting mainland China and the international community. Through research platforms such as the Centre for Precision and Regenerative Medicine Research, MUST will actively expand partnerships with leading universities and research institutions worldwide, promote innovation in medical education, scientific research, talent development, and research translation, and contribute to the development of the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area as an international science and technology innovation hub.

Figure 4. Professor Paul Kwong-Hang Tam, Vice President of MUST, and Dr. Bo Li, Assistant Professor at the Centre for Precision and Regenerative Medicine Research, together with distinguished guests at the event.

entry.title: MUST Assistant Professor Bo Li Invited to Contribute to Paediatrics Development Planning in Liaoning Province

link.title: MUST Assistant Professor Bo Li Invited to Contribute to Paediatrics Development Planning in Liaoning Province

entry.content:
Recently, Assistant Professor Bo Li from the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC) at Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST) was invited by Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University to attend an academic event in Shenyang related to the development planning of paediatrics in Liaoning Province. He delivered a thematic presentation and joined clinical and research experts from across the province in discussions on paediatric discipline development, scientific innovation, talent cultivation, and clinical translation.

Figure 1. Assistant Professor Bo Li delivers a thematic presentation at the Liaoning Province paediatrics development planning meeting at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University.

The meeting was organized in response to the healthcare and academic development needs of paediatrics in Liaoning Province. Discussions focused on strengthening leading paediatric specialties, improving the diagnosis and treatment of major childhood diseases, integrating clinical resources, cultivating medical talent, and promoting interdisciplinary collaboration. The event aimed to further consolidate paediatric clinical and research expertise across the province and enhance the coordinated development of clinical care, education, and research.

During the meeting, Assistant Professor Li presented his research in neonatal and paediatric intestinal diseases, intestinal stem cells, organoids, and regenerative medicine. He introduced the research team’s broader efforts to use stem cell and organoid technologies to investigate intestinal injury and repair, tissue microenvironment regulation, and regenerative therapeutic strategies. From the perspective of integrating fundamental research with clinical needs, the presentation also explored the potential application of regenerative medicine technologies in severe neonatal and paediatric gastrointestinal diseases.

During the event, Assistant Professor Li held in-depth discussions with experts from the paediatrics and paediatric surgery teams at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University. The discussions covered neonatal intestinal diseases, congenital gastrointestinal disorders, fetal and paediatric disease research, postoperative tissue repair, and life-course health management. The two sides also explored potential models of collaboration involving clinical sample resources, training of young researchers, student exchanges, and joint research projects.

Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University has a strong clinical and research foundation in paediatrics and paediatric surgery, together with extensive resources in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood diseases. The Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre at MUST continues to advance the integration of stem cells, organoids, tissue engineering, and disease modelling. The two institutions therefore have complementary strengths in the mechanistic study of major paediatric diseases and the development of regenerative therapeutic strategies.

The exchange strengthened academic links between MUST and Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University and created new opportunities for MUST to participate in regional paediatric discipline development and expand high-level clinical research collaboration in mainland China. By combining MUST’s internationally connected research platforms with Liaoning Province’s extensive paediatric clinical resources, the two sides may further promote multidisciplinary, multicentre, and cross-regional collaboration, while accelerating the translation of research findings into improved diagnosis and treatment for childhood diseases.

Moving forward, the MUST research team will continue to address the clinical needs associated with major neonatal and paediatric diseases, strengthen collaboration with leading children’s medical centres and clinical specialties in mainland China, and promote deeper integration of fundamental research, clinical resources, talent development, and translational innovation, contributing to the high-quality development of paediatrics and the advancement of child health.

entry.title: Assistant Professor Bo Li Presents at ISSCR 2026 Annual Meeting in Montreal

link.title: Assistant Professor Bo Li Presents at ISSCR 2026 Annual Meeting in Montreal

entry.content:
Assistant Professor Bo Li from the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC) at Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST) was invited to attend and deliver an oral presentation at the International Society for Stem Cell Research (ISSCR) 2026 Annual Meeting, held in Montreal, Canada, from July 8 to 11, 2026. He shared the latest research advances from his team in the fields of intestinal organoids, neonatal intestinal injury, and regenerative medicine.

Assistant Professor Li presented in the symposium session “Modulating the Tissue Niche for Therapeutic Success.” His presentation focused on the regulation of tissue microenvironments, intestinal repair, and regenerative therapeutic strategies. He introduced his research team’s efforts using organoid-based approaches and regenerative technologies to explore novel treatment strategies for severe neonatal intestinal diseases.

ISSCR is one of the leading global organizations in the field of stem cell biology and regenerative medicine. Its annual meeting brings together experts and researchers worldwide in areas including stem cell biology, organoids, tissue engineering, disease modeling, and cell therapy, showcasing the latest advances in both fundamental research and clinical translation.

During the meeting, Assistant Professor Li also exchanged ideas with researchers from different countries and regions on intestinal stem cells, organoid technologies, the tissue microenvironment, and regenerative therapies, while exploring opportunities for future scientific collaboration.

This oral presentation showcased MUST’s research progress in stem cells, organoids, and regenerative medicine for paediatric diseases, further strengthening the international academic visibility of the University’s related research. Moving forward, the research team will continue to integrate fundamental regenerative medicine research with clinical needs and explore innovative therapeutic strategies for severe neonatal and paediatric intestinal diseases.

Figure 1. Assistant Professor Bo Li delivers an oral presentation on intestinal organoids, neonatal intestinal injury, and regenerative medicine at the ISSCR 2026 Annual Meeting in Montreal, Canada.

entry.title: Lab Meeting at the MUST Innovation Technology Research Institute in Hengqin

link.title: Lab Meeting at the MUST Innovation Technology Research Institute in Hengqin

entry.content:
On June 15, 2026, our lab meeting was held at the MUST Innovation Technology Research Institute in the Hengqin-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone. During the meeting, we discussed recent progress in our ongoing projects, reviewed experimental plans, and aligned the next steps for our research on intestinal disease, organoid models, and regenerative medicine.

It was a productive opportunity for the team to exchange ideas, strengthen collaboration, and continue building our research platform in Hengqin. The Innovation Technology Research Institute provides an excellent environment for cutting-edge research and fosters interdisciplinary collaboration between Macau and the mainland.

The meeting covered a wide range of topics, including updates on biliary atresia studies, intestinal organoid development, liver fibrosis models, and tissue injury repair mechanisms. Team members presented their latest data and received constructive feedback from colleagues, contributing to the refinement of ongoing experimental strategies.

As our research presence in Hengqin continues to grow, this gathering marks another important step in building a robust platform for translational medicine research in the Greater Bay Area.

Figure 1. Group photo of the Bo Li Laboratory team at the MUST Innovation Technology Research Institute in the Hengqin-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone, June 15, 2026.

Figure 2. Team members engage in discussions on biliary atresia studies, intestinal organoid models, and liver fibrosis research during the lab meeting at the Hengqin research facility.

entry.title: PRMRC Team Participates in the Academic Conference of the Abdominal Surgery Group of the Chinese Medical Association Pediatric Surgery Branch

link.title: PRMRC Team Participates in the Academic Conference of the Abdominal Surgery Group of the Chinese Medical Association Pediatric Surgery Branch

entry.content:
Recently, the Academic Conference of the Abdominal Surgery Group of the Pediatric Surgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Association was held in Guangzhou. Professor Yan Chen, Assistant Director of the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre (PRMRC) at Macau University of Science and Technology, and Assistant Professor Bo Li, together with team members, attended the conference and engaged in academic exchanges with pediatric surgery experts from across China. The discussions focused on biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, pediatric intestinal diseases, and translational medicine.

The conference centered on clinical and research advances in pediatric abdominal surgery, with dedicated sessions covering hepatosplenic diseases, portal hypertension and pancreatic diseases, biliary diseases, biliary atresia, Hirschsprung disease, anorectal malformations, and rare anorectal and abdominal surgical conditions. Pediatric surgeons and researchers from children’s hospitals, general hospitals, and university-affiliated hospitals across the country shared recent progress in clinical management, surgical innovation, clinical research, and translational studies.

During the conference, Yingying He, a student supervised by Assistant Professor Bo Li, delivered an oral presentation entitled “Cholestatic Injury-Induced Intestinal Fibrosis and Epithelial Dysfunction May Contribute to Post-Kasai Cholangitis in Biliary Atresia.” The presentation introduced the team’s recent findings on mechanisms related to post-Kasai cholangitis, intestinal fibrosis, and epithelial dysfunction in biliary atresia. This study provides new insights into the pathogenesis of postoperative complications in biliary atresia from the perspective of liver-intestine interaction and tissue injury repair.

Professor Yan Chen was invited to chair a session on biliary atresia, where he joined participating experts in discussions on the diagnosis and treatment of biliary atresia, immunopathological mechanisms, organoid research, post-Kasai management, and clinical translation. Assistant Professor Bo Li also exchanged views with experts on biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, pediatric intestinal diseases, tissue injury repair, and potential collaborations involving clinical samples and translational research.

Following the conference, Assistant Professor Bo Li and colleagues visited Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University for further academic exchange. They met with Professor Kai Wu and his pediatric surgery team to discuss potential collaborations in pediatric intestinal diseases, necrotizing enterocolitis, tissue injury repair, and translational medicine. Both sides exchanged views on future cooperation in clinical sample resources, disease models, research grant applications, and talent exchange, laying a foundation for PRMRC to further expand its pediatric medicine collaboration network in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

This participation further strengthened the connection between PRMRC and leading pediatric surgery experts and clinical centers in China. It also reflected the Centre’s continued development in biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, pediatric intestinal diseases, tissue injury repair, and translational medicine. Moving forward, PRMRC will continue to leverage its research platforms to promote close integration between basic research and clinical needs, strengthen collaboration with leading pediatric medical centers, and advance mechanistic and translational research in pediatric surgical diseases.

Figure 1. Yingying He, a master’s student supervised by Assistant Professor Bo Li, delivers an oral presentation on biliary atresia post-Kasai cholangitis mechanisms at the CMA Pediatric Surgery conference in Guangzhou.

Figure 2. Assistant Professor Bo Li discusses potential collaborations in pediatric intestinal diseases, necrotizing enterocolitis, and tissue injury repair with Professor Kai Wu and his pediatric surgery team at Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University.

The discussions focused on biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, pediatric intestinal diseases, and translational medicine.

entry.title: MUST Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre at the International Conference on Hirschsprung Disease in Genoa

link.title: MUST Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre at the International Conference on Hirschsprung Disease in Genoa

entry.content:
On April 12, 2026, Vice President of Macau University of Science and Technology (MUST), Chair Prof. Paul Kwong Hang Tam, led faculty members and student representatives from the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre to participate in the International Conference on Hirschsprung Disease (HSCR), held in Genoa, Italy.

Organized by the International Consortium on the Genetics of Hirschsprung Disease, the meeting brought together distinguished scholars from the Americas, Europe, Asia, and other regions. During the conference, Vice President Tam delivered a keynote lecture highlighting the major scientific contributions of human genetics research to the field of Hirschsprung disease, the key challenges currently facing the field, and future directions for development. The conference focused on in-depth exchanges across multiple areas, including the genetic basis of HSCR, as well as its clinical and surgical management, systematically showcasing the latest research advances. These discussions underscored that HSCR research is evolving from single-gene and candidate-gene studies toward more comprehensive approaches involving genomics, transcriptomics, and disease stratification, thereby opening new directions for precision diagnosis, mechanistic investigation, and individualized intervention.

At the conference, Assistant Professor Bo Li from the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre delivered an academic presentation entitled “HAEC and stromal-epithelial regenerative cross-talk.” Drawing on the team’s research foundation in the intestinal microenvironment, stromal remodeling, and regenerative repair, the presentation introduced new ideas regarding HSCR-associated enterocolitis and impaired tissue repair.

Earlier, Assistant Professor Li also attended the ENS 2026 Leuven meeting in Belgium, where he engaged in extensive discussions with international colleagues on frontier topics including enteric nervous system development, Hirschsprung disease, the pathogenesis of HAEC, and regenerative medicine.

This series of conference participations further enhanced the international visibility and engagement of the Precision Regenerative Medicine Research Centre under the Faculty of Medicine at MUST in the fields of intestinal development and regenerative medicine. It also strengthened collaborative ties with international peers in HSCR genetics, disease mechanisms, and translational research, laying a solid foundation for further integrating related research at MUST into the global academic network and increasing its academic influence.
